bibliographic.title: Large language models in patient education for brain tumors: opportunities, risks, and ethical considerations
bibliographic.authors: Rafail C. Christodoulou, Platon S. Papageorgiou, Ana Carolina Lucio Pereira, Elena E. Solomou, Sokratis G. Papageorgiou, Evros Vassiliou, Michalis F. Georgiou
bibliographic.citation_apa: Christodoulou, R. C., Papageorgiou, P. S., Lucio Pereira, A. C., Solomou, E. E., Papageorgiou, S. G., Vassiliou, E., & Georgiou, M. F. (2026). Large language models in patient education for brain tumors: opportunities, risks, and ethical considerations. Frontiers in Oncology, 16, 1795441. https://doi.org/10.3389/fonc.2026.1795441

methodology.study_design: narrative review with literature synthesis using controlled vocabulary and keyword search for transformer-based LLM studies after 2020
methodology.sample_description: Evidence from neuro-oncology, radiology, and digital health literature on LLMs for patient education in brain tumors
methodology.technology_context: LLMs and AI chatbots for explaining imaging results, diagnoses, and treatment options in patient-centered language under clinician supervision

eligibility.decision_rationale: Narrative review focused primarily on LLM-supported patient education in neuro-oncology, but it explicitly addresses governance, oversight, clinician supervision, privacy, ethical risks, and proposes a clinician-guided framework for responsible integration. Relevant to regulated LLM use and human oversight, yet not centered on conversational governance as the main object of study.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only partial full text provided; number of included studies and complete review methodology not visible in supplied excerpts.

appraisal.notes: Clear narrative-review objective and ethical framing are present. Search terms and post-2020 inclusion criterion are described, but the supplied text does not report the number of included studies or a full critical appraisal protocol for source studies.

cerqual.explanation: The review coherently links LLM opportunities and risks in regulated healthcare education and proposes supervised integration, but available excerpts are incomplete and the narrative design limits methodological certainty.

coding.theme: Responsible LLM use for patient education in regulated neuro-oncology settings
coding.subtheme: Clinician-guided framework with governance and oversight

synthesis.main_claim: Under clinician supervision, LLMs may improve patient understanding and engagement in brain tumor care, but safe implementation requires structured governance, oversight, and ethical alignment.
synthesis.contribution: Synthesizes neuro-oncology, radiology, and digital health evidence on LLM-assisted patient education and proposes a clinician-guided framework for responsible integration.
synthesis.limitations: Supplied text is partial; narrative review design; brain tumor domain specificity; exact corpus size and appraisal of primary studies are unclear.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence on governance, oversight, ethical risks, and supervised conversational LLM deployment in regulated healthcare, especially patient education contexts.

evidence.claim: Study is a narrative review on LLMs in brain tumor patient education.
evidence.excerpt: Objective: This narrative review evaluates the role of large language models (LLMs) in supporting patient education for individuals with brain tumors.

evidence.claim: Article addresses governance and oversight for safe LLM implementation.
evidence.excerpt: Safe implementation will require structured governance, oversight, and alignment with ethical standards.
A clinician-guided framework for responsible integration is proposed.

evidence.claim: LLMs should be used under clinician supervision as educational support tools.
evidence.excerpt: When used under clinician supervision as educational support tools, LLMs may enhance patient understanding and engagement in brain tumor care.

evidence.claim: Review discusses key LLM risks including privacy and ethical challenges.
evidence.excerpt: Key limitations are also discussed, including hallucinations, output variability, overtrust, data privacy concerns, and ethical challenges.

evidence.claim: Specific LLMs such as ChatGPT-4 are discussed.
evidence.excerpt: none of the patient materials on brain tumor prognosis, whether online or generated by ChatGPT-4, met the recommended readability standards

evidence.claim: Search strategy targeted transformer-based LLM literature after 2020.
evidence.excerpt: ensuring inclusion of contemporary studies on transformer-based LLMs after 2020.

evidence.claim: Search terms included LLM, ChatGPT, GPT-4, patient education, and brain tumor terms.
evidence.excerpt: including variations of: "large language model," "ChatGPT," "GPT-4," "artificial intelligence," "patient education," "health literacy," "oncology communication," "brain tumor," "glioma,"

evidence.claim: AI chatbots enable scalable conversational patient interaction.
evidence.excerpt: while a doctor can see only a limited number of patients, an AI chatbot can interact with many patients simultaneously throughout the day

evidence.claim: Framework figure describes LLM-assisted education under clinician supervision.
evidence.excerpt: Large language models transform radiotherapy and imaging data into simplified, personalized, and accessible patient-centered educational content under clinician supervision

evidence.claim: Article is peer reviewed and published in Frontiers in Oncology.
